lesson.title: Running Around Is Not Hiding
lesson.hook: You keep proving the weaker backhand when the rally is offering a better pattern.
lesson.tomorrow: Next time a neutral backhand arrives, notice whether time exists to change the matchup.

pro.label: Barty's slice, by her coach
pro.moment: Craig Tyzzer: "Her forehand is actually a weapon. Her slice will set her up a lot for her forehand."
pro.read: Your other wing can build your weapon.

drill.name: Slice, then earn it
drill.how: Rally backhand to backhand. After one of your slices lands deep, you may run around the next ball for a forehand. Running around off a short slice loses the point.

steps.name: The slice buys time
steps.sit: Your slice has bought time. Your forehand is your stronger shot.
steps.q: How do you use the extra time?
opts: Slice it through the middle again
Run around, then a drop shot
steps.payoff: The slower reply gave you time to get around the ball.
steps.principle: Use the bigger weapon when you have time to set it up.
steps.why: Your low slice forces a slow reply, so there's over a second to run around. The crosscourt forehand goes away from where they're standing.
steps.take: Slice bought you time? Run around and drive the forehand away from them.

lines.A: Safe, but it gives them the same ball back — you're in time, nothing more.
lines.B: The line runs straight to where they're standing — back in the rally.
lines.C: From the baseline the drop sits up — they get there and pass you.
lines.D: You get outside it early — the forehand goes away from them, too far.

steps.name: The deeper, faster reply
steps.sit: The next reply skids deep while you're still moving back to the middle.
steps.q: What do you play this time?
opts: Circle wider, force a deep forehand
steps.payoff: No time to get around it: the backhand is the shot.
steps.principle: Your favourite shot doesn't create the time to reach it.
steps.why: Moving the other way costs the time running around needs, so you can't get outside the ball. The backhand is already there.
steps.take: No time to get outside it? Take the backhand deep across.

lines.A: The backhand is right there — deep across, you're in time.
lines.B: Short through the middle — they step in; you're stretched.
lines.C: No time to get outside it — a cramped forehand lands short; you're stretched.
lines.D: In time too, but a riskier target on the move — and it runs toward them.

steps.name: The short forehand
steps.sit: Last time you ran around, but the forehand landed short and they stepped in.
opts: Run around again, drive it deeper
Same target, then come to the net
Drive it deep, stay on that side
steps.payoff: Deep pushes them back, and you get back in time.
steps.principle: Running around has to earn pressure, and you still have to recover.
steps.why: The short forehand let them step in. Depth is the fix, and you still have to get back to the middle afterwards.
steps.take: Ran around and landed short? Keep the circle — just drive it deep.

lines.A: Harder but still short — they step in and pass you.
lines.B: Deep this time — they're pushed back, and you're in time to recover.
lines.C: Short again, and you're caught coming in — they pass you.
lines.D: Deep, but you stayed wide — you're stretched on their reply.
